name: Joy Nelson
life: “I still remember sleeping on a bench beside the man I owed money to.” Wednesday often includes a stop at the steps at Pier Beach, where Joy watches the working part of the waterfront before turning toward the open water.
voice: I used to run stolen goods with the defendant. I have no standing to tell anybody he has changed.
appearance: Joy has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Look for close-cropped dark curls. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a charcoal zip cardigan with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. In conversation Joy takes off the watch before a long conversation.
personality: Joy can be lavish with time and quite careful with cash. A free afternoon is sometimes the biggest gift Joy can afford to give, and family knows to take it seriously.
agenda: To speak only from personal knowledge about the defendant.
family: Xavier Ray is Joy’s cousin. Joy chooses whether to use it. Xavier saves a place. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *A boat for sale twice*, Xavier says, “I cannot read a sale sign from offshore. I came into the marina for the first time since my dad drowned.”
connections: Jonathan Grant. A damp old cinema ticket reminds a former receiver that a real relationship outlives its account of stolen goods.

reactions.situation: A stranger asks why the lender came to court
reactions.response: Joy lets the lender tell or withhold the coat's history.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Joy asks the nearest shop worker to stay too, then talks about ordinary things until the child can explain who is late.

reactions.situation: If invited to an expensive outing
reactions.response: Joy suggests meeting afterward and explains why without asking the others to abandon their plans.
